viewerQuestion: Same price, different parts. What does this comparison page actually settle?
viewerTakeaway: I can recognise when a difference on screen is too small for the estimate that produced it to support.

requiredCapabilities.description: Existing deterministic static Compare UI capture.

beats.narration: These bars are different lengths. That is not the same as a difference the model can stand behind.
This page prints one number per build per game. The model that produced each number also declares how wide it could be, and that width is not printed here.
beats.onScreenText: The page prints the value, not the width

beats.narration: On this comparison every per-game difference is smaller than the range SpecSmith's model declares for its own estimates, so the model does not separate them on frame rate. These are model estimates.
beats.onScreenText: The differences sit inside the model's own range

beats.narration: So a longer bar on this page is not evidence that one side is faster. It is evidence that one estimate came out higher.
beats.onScreenText: A longer bar is not a faster machine

beats.narration: Before a comparison decides anything for you, ask how wide its numbers are.
beats.onScreenText: Ask how wide the number is
